summary: A Reuters roundup of weekend European football on 30 September 2023. Bayern Munich came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 at RB Leipzig, Real Madrid beat Girona 3-0 to top LaLiga, Lautaro Martínez scored four off the bench for Inter, Milan beat Lazio 2-0, and Monaco beat Marseille 3-2 to go top of Ligue 1.
one_line: Reuters roundup: Bayern draw at Leipzig, Real Madrid top LaLiga, Martínez scores four for Inter, Milan and Monaco win.
key_facts: Bayern Munich came from two goals down to draw 2-2 at RB Leipzig, with second-half goals from Leroy Sané and Harry Kane.
Bayern are third in the Bundesliga on 14 points, two behind leaders Bayer Leverkusen; it was their second draw of the season.
Harry Kane scored his eighth league goal from a 57th-minute penalty; only Erling Haaland, for Borussia Dortmund, scored more in his first six Bundesliga games, with nine goals.
Leipzig's goals came from Loïs Openda in the 20th minute and Castello Lukeba after Sven Ulreich misjudged a corner.
Real Madrid beat Girona 3-0 with goals from Joselu, Aurélien Tchouméni and Jude Bellingham, going top of LaLiga on 21 points from eight games, one ahead of Barcelona.
Vinícius Jr was substituted in the 68th minute in his first start after a thigh muscle injury.
Lautaro Martínez came off the bench to score all four goals as Inter won 4-0 at Salernitana, scoring four goals in 27 minutes after coming on nine minutes after the break.
Martínez has nine goals in seven league games and is Serie A's top scorer; Inter had lost at San Siro to Sassuolo earlier.
Inter lead Serie A on 18 points, level with Milan, who beat Lazio 2-0 with second-half goals from Christian Pulisic and Noah Okafor.
Rafael Leão, 24, provided two assists for Milan, whose midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek limped off in the first half with a possible groin problem.
AS Monaco beat Marseille 3-2 to go top of Ligue 1, with two goals from Maghnes Akliouche and one from Folarin Balogun.
Marseille, who appointed Gennaro Gattuso as coach this week, led twice through Iliman Ndiaye (30 seconds) and Samuel Gigot (18th minute).
